text: Tri-City Healthcare District is entering a new era. Sharp HealthCare now operates Tri-City Medical Center under a long-term partnership that promises major investments, expanded services, and greater financial stability.

The District Board must ensure these changes serve North County residents while preserving transparency, public stewardship, and local accountability. After 12 years representing Oceanside residents on the City Council, I bring experience in strategic planning, financial oversight, and collaborative decision-making - skills that are needed in the new environment.

Tri-City Medical Center is vital to North County and I will work to ensure it continues delivering safe, reliable, high-quality care while building a stronger and more sustainable future for our community. I will safeguard public resources by promoting financial strength, transparency, and responsible oversight. I will hold the Sharp partnership accountable for its commitments to modernize the hospital, improve operations, restore and expand critical services, and strengthen long-term resilience. I will protect local accountability by ensuring the community has a strong voice in decisions affecting patients, families, employees, and taxpayers
I will provide steady, constructive leadership grounded in collaboration, careful planning, and measurable results.
I would be honored to earn your trust and your vote.

text: For 50 years, I have loved being a Registered Nurse. I moved from Chicago to CA and found Oceanside in 2002. I fell in love with this harbor community. My home came next in 2004 in Oceanside District 2. Running for the Tri-City Healthcare district board of directors allows me to demonstrate my desire for quality services locally. When elected, I will advocate for availability of services, resources, communication, and partnering with this community.

I am committed to stewardship, with desirable results for families and patients. Since 2002, I have worked full time in our community with providers, neighbors, and patients to locate appropriate quality medical resources based on individual goals and return to best health outcomes with quality of life.

As of mother of 3 children with 7 grandchildren, I understand the importance of local healthcare. Recently, working as a Nurse Case Manager, my experience has acquainted me with every hospital in San Diego County. I have worked at 3 district hospitals in North San Diego County. This has provided me with knowledge of hospital administration and home care services. I want to see that our tax dollars for Tri-City healthcare district are impactful for generations to come.

text: My name is Kayla Lauriano, and I’m running for the Tri-City Healthcare Board of Directors because our community deserves leadership that understands healthcare from the bedside, not just the boardroom.

Born at Tri-City, raised on Camp Pendleton, and an Oceanside resident for more than 20 years, I’ve proudly served our community as a registered nurse for 17 years. My career has focused on women’s health, including high-risk Labor and Delivery, Birth Center, Antepartum, Postpartum, and Level III NICU. I’ve cared for families through life’s most joyful moments and greatest challenges, reinforcing the importance of compassionate, patient-centered leadership.

I’m running to bring a frontline perspective to the board. I understand the challenges facing healthcare today, including workforce shortages, access to care, rising costs, and the social factors that influence health. Every patient deserves safe, culturally responsive, patient-centered care.
If elected, I will advocate for expanding access, investing in our healthcare workforce, promoting transparency and fiscal responsibility, and strengthening community partnerships.
I’m not running because I’m interested in politics—I’m running because I believe service doesn’t end when you leave the bedside. It evolves.
It would be an honor to earn your vote.
Your Nurse. Your Neighbor. Your Voice.
